27 Which frequency of electromagnetic radiation could be ultraviolet?
A
1.0 × 106
Hz
B
1.0 × 109
Hz
C
1.0 × 1012
Hz
D
1.0 × 1015
Hz

hints: Notice the four frequencies increase by factors of 1000 from $10^6 \text{ Hz}$ to $10^{15} \text{ Hz}$ - recall where visible light sits on this scale at about $4$ to $8 \times 10^{14} \text{ Hz}$.
Recall the order of increasing frequency in the electromagnetic spectrum: radio, microwave, infrared, visible, ultraviolet, X-ray - so ultraviolet must be higher frequency than visible light.
Check with $c = f\lambda$ using $c = 3.0 \times 10^8 \text{ m s}^{-1}$: only one given frequency gives $\lambda$ around $10^{-7} \text{ m}$, the ultraviolet wavelength range.
walkthrough: Identify the position of ultraviolet: it has higher frequency and shorter wavelength than visible light, but lower frequency than X-rays.
Recall visible light has wavelength about $400$ to $700 \text{ nm}$, so frequency $f = c/\lambda$ is about $4 \times 10^{14} \text{ Hz}$ to $8 \times 10^{14} \text{ Hz}$.
Ultraviolet must therefore have $f$ greater than about $8 \times 10^{14} \text{ Hz}$, typically $10^{15} \text{ Hz}$ to $10^{16} \text{ Hz}$.

Test the largest value: $f = 1.0 \times 10^{15} \text{ Hz}$ gives $\lambda = c/f = 3.0 \times 10^8 / 1.0 \times 10^{15} = 3.0 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m} = 300 \text{ nm}$, which lies in the ultraviolet range.

The other values give much longer wavelengths: $10^6 \text{ Hz}$ gives $300 \text{ m}$ (radio), $10^9 \text{ Hz}$ gives $0.3 \text{ m}$ (microwave), $10^{12} \text{ Hz}$ gives $0.3 \text{ mm}$ (infrared).
Only $1.0 \times 10^{15} \text{ Hz}$ fits ultraviolet. This is option D.

A.explanation: A frequency of $1.0 \times 10^6 \text{ Hz}$ is in the radio wave region, far lower in frequency than visible light and ultraviolet.

B.explanation: A frequency of $1.0 \times 10^9 \text{ Hz}$ is in the microwave region, still much lower in frequency than infrared, visible light and ultraviolet.

C.explanation: A frequency of $1.0 \times 10^{12} \text{ Hz}$ is in the infrared region, just below visible light in frequency and below ultraviolet.

D.explanation: A frequency of $1.0 \times 10^{15} \text{ Hz}$ is just above visible light frequency, giving a wavelength of about $300 \text{ nm}$, which is ultraviolet.
